name: The Living Stained Glass Cathedral of Seasons
description: A cathedral grown from living trees whose leaves are stained glass, changing color with seasons. Sunlight paints the forest floor with shifting sacred geometry that migrates across the year -- spring's pastel mandalas, summer's blazing gold, autumn's amber fractals, winter's ice-crystal blues.
prompt: A massive cathedral-like space formed by ancient trees grown in architectural arches. Their leaves are literal stained glass -- thick, leaded, jewel-toned panels that photosynthesize light. Spring: pastel pink/green leaves casting rose mandalas on moss floor. Summer: blazing ruby/gold/amber panels projecting intense sacred geometry. Autumn: amber/orange/red fractal patterns. Winter: clear ice-crystal leaves casting blue snowflake patterns. The 'floor' is living moss that glows where light touches. Branches form flying buttresses. No roof needed -- canopy is the art. Hyper-detailed botanical accuracy meets gothic architecture. Seasonal transition captured in single image.
caption: A cathedral not built, but grown. 🌳🕊️ Its leaves are stained glass, its light a prayer in color. The floor remembers every season's shadow. Come back in three months -- the sermon will be completely different.
